title: Computed Keys and Shorthand Check
description: Property shorthand and computed keys in object literals.

questions.explanation: Shorthand `{ name }` means `{ name: name }`. `[field]` evaluates to the string `"role"`.

questions.prompt: What does `{ name, age }` mean when `name` and `age` are variables?

options.text: Same as `{ name: name, age: age }`
Creates keys from the string values of the variables

questions.explanation: Property shorthand reuses the variable name as both key and value.

questions.prompt: Given `const key = "name"`, which literal creates a property named `"name"`?
questions.explanation: `{ key: "Ada" }` always creates a property literally named `key`. Computed keys use `[key]`.

options.text: Only when the property is first read

questions.explanation: The expression inside `[...]` runs when the literal is evaluated, and the resulting string/symbol becomes the key.
Template literals inside computed keys are evaluated, so the key becomes `userId`.
